cues: Spreading charge lowers energy, so the phenoxide ion is unusually stable, and phenol gives up its proton more readily.
In the ethoxide ion there is no ring to spread into.
The charge is stuck on oxygen, and the ethyl group pushes even more electron density onto it.
A second reason: in phenol itself, oxygen's lone pair already leaks into the ring, so the oxygen holds the O H electrons more tightly, and the proton leaves more easily.
text: Spreading charge lowers energy, so the phenoxide ion is unusually stable, and phenol gives up its proton more readily. In the ethoxide ion there is no ring to spread into. The charge is stuck on oxygen, and the ethyl group pushes even more electron density onto it. So ethanol is far weaker. A second reason: in phenol itself, oxygen's lone pair already leaks into the ring, so the oxygen holds the O H electrons more tightly, and the proton leaves more easily.
